title: Automated Alert Suppression and Steering Runbook for Region Cutover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
Redwood operates multi-region inference fleets. During planned and unplanned region cutovers we see a surge of transient SLO alerts (latency p50/p95 skew, model timeouts, circuit breaker tripping) which generates noisy pages, delays failover coordination, and increases MTTA. Current runbooks are mostly manual: engineers must mute routes, update routing policies, and coordinate cross-region cache invalidation.

Goals:
1) Reduce on-call noise during region cutovers by automatically suppressing low-value alerts while preserving high-fidelity SLO breach notifications.
2) Provide a deterministic, automated steering sequence that executes safe failover steps (route weight shift, KV prefix pinning, circuit breaker scaling) with manual-confirm pause points.
3) Integrate suppression and steering into team runbooks and incident automation tooling so runbook steps are executable from the Console and via Slack/Opsbot.

Non-goals:
- Replace human judgment for catastrophic failures. Critical region-wide failures still require human escalation.
- Full automation of model fallback selection (future work).

Proposed approach:
A) Adaptive Suppressor: a short-lived, policy-driven suppression layer that uses correlated signals to suppress noisy symptom alerts for an affected region while allowing top-level SLO breach alerts to pass. Rules:
  - If regional routing change event (source=router/scale-controller) detected AND p50 latency increased but p99 stable -> suppress low-severity latency alerts for 5–15 minutes.
  - If circuit-breaker rate > 10% OR 5xx rate > threshold -> allow alert through (no suppression).
  - Suppressor exposes a 'suppression-mode' tag in telemetry for post-incident analysis.

B) Steering Runbook (automated steps + manual gates):
  1. Pre-cutover checks (traffic snapshots, KV hot prefixes, active batch sizes).
  2. Enter suppression-mode (API call) to reduce noise.
  3. Execute weight-shift in 10% increments with 1-minute stabilization windows; monitor failure and latency metrics.
  4. On circuit-breaker activation: auto-scale dedicated pool or pause weight shift and notify SRE.
  5. Post-cutover verification and graceful suppression lift.

C) Console & Opsbot integration: runbook actions exposed as buttons in Console (Start cutover, Pause, Abort) and as slash commands in Slack with audit logging. Every automated action emits an annotated event to the audit log and to the incident timeline.

Acceptance criteria:
- When executing a test cutover on the staging fleet, noise volume (number of pages to oncall) drops by >= 70% relative to the baseline while high-severity SLO breach pages are still produced.
- Automated steering completes at expected cadence with no silent failures in >= 90% of test runs.
- All steps are reversible via Console within 5 minutes and leave sufficient telemetry for postmortem.

Metrics to track:
- pages_per_cutover (baseline vs with suppressor),
- false_suppression_rate (% of suppressed alerts that should have fired),
- steering_success_rate (percent runs that complete without manual abort),
- mean_time_to_recover (MTTR) for cutover incidents.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Conservative suppression rules reduce noise but may delay detection of slow-degrading impacts. We prioritize preserving p99/p95-driven pages and error-rate alerts.
- Tight integration with routing controller required; adds surface area to revert logic. Decided to add explicit manual gates on abort paths to reduce blast radius.

Deliverables:
- Adaptive suppressor service + policy templates,
- Steering runbook implementation (console actions + opsbot),
- Staging cutover test harness + dashboards,
- PRD + runbook doc in Confluence (linked below).
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Triage complete. Drafted approach and acceptance criteria. Scoped to horizontal failure modes first (routing/caching).

2026-02-25 - Marco Liu: Started spike to validate event signals from router and circuit-breaker. Found that router emits sticky events at /events/routing with delay ~3s. Will add buffering to avoid flapping.

2026-03-01 - Sofia Martinez (Design review): UX for runbook buttons in Console reviewed. Suggested a confirmation modal that surfaces current suppression policy and expected impact numbers. Created design ticket DES-739 for modal copy.

2026-03-03 - Evan Brooks (SRE): Ran staging cutover; observed 65% reduction in noisy pages with naive suppression. Need to tune rule that allowed p50-only suppression; raised risk of delayed cache-miss cascades.

2026-03-06 - Marco Liu: Implemented conservative policy variant: do not suppress if KV hot-prefix misses exceed 1% during window. Deployed to staging (link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4123).
2026-03-08 - QA: Integration tests for steering cadence added. One failure remained where abort path left route weights inconsistent; patch in PR 4128.
2026-03-10 - Security review: Confirmed audit events include masked customer identifiers. No further changes required. (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/ENG-86753+Runbook).

2026-03-12 - Marco Liu: Merged suppressor core and Console action UI behind feature flag. Rollout schedule: staged to 10% of org staging runs this week, full internal rollout next week. Next: open load-test and SLO sensitivity tuning session with Product and SRE.
